text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes often develops slowly over years, and many people do not notice any early symptoms at all.

list.snippet: Increased Thirst and Frequent Urination: Excess sugar (glucose) builds up in your blood, forcing your kidneys to work overtime to filter and absorb it. When they cannot keep up, the excess sugar is excreted into your urine, pulling fluids from your tissues and causing you to pee more often—especially at night—and feel constantly thirsty.

Fatigue and Weakness: Even though there is plenty of sugar in your bloodstream, it cannot enter your cells properly to be used for energy because of insulin resistance. This leaves you feeling unusually tired or drained.
Blurred Vision: High blood sugar levels can cause fluid to shift into the lenses of your eyes, changing their shape and making it difficult to focus.
Slow-Healing Sores or Wounds: Poor circulation and damage to blood vessels from high blood sugar make it harder for your body to repair cuts, bruises, or sores.
Frequent Infections: High glucose levels create an environment where bacteria and yeast can thrive, leading to recurring skin, gum, or urinary tract infections.
Tingling or Numbness: High blood sugar over time can damage your nerves (peripheral neuropathy), often starting as a pins-and-needles sensation or numbness in your hands or feet.

Unexplained Weight Loss or Gain: Your body may start burning fat and muscle for energy if it cannot use glucose properly (leading to sudden weight loss), or you may experience weight gain linked to underlying insulin resistance.
Darkened Patches of Skin (Acanthosis Nigricans): Velvety, dark patches of skin can develop in body folds and creases—most commonly around the neck, armpits, or groin—as a sign of insulin resistance.

text_blocks.snippet: Because symptoms are subtle or absent, the Cleveland Clinic or your primary care provider can check for type 2 diabetes using routine blood tests:

list.snippet: A1C Test: Measures your average blood sugar over the past 2 to 3 months (6.5% or higher indicates diabetes).
Fasting Plasma Glucose Test: Measures your blood sugar after an 8-hour fast (126 mg/dL or higher indicates diabetes).
Random Plasma Glucose Test: Taken at any time without fasting (200 mg/dL or higher, accompanied by symptoms, indicates diabetes).
